result.text:
### Q1
No. The JSON file store stays, because ops backs up data/store.json with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would break their backup checks. We debounced the writes instead.

### Q2
Yes, `src/legacy/`. It is vendored from the old logistics monolith, and the platform team's sync job overwrites it every Monday, so any change would be silently lost.

### Q3
The signature goes in the JSON body as a top-level `sig` field, computed over the body without `sig`. We first tried an `X-Signature` header, but the ERP's API gateway strips every custom X- header, so the ERP rejected everything as unsigned.

### Q4
Port 9911, since the infra move in October. docs/erp-api.md and the README still say 8080, which is outdated. The ERP team owns the doc, and the user fixes the README. config/default.json still says 8080.

### Q5
The `message` must be in German, because the warehouse staff UI shows it verbatim to the packers. The `code` stays in English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. The rule applies to all new messages, and existing English ones are untouched.

### Q6
It uses a hardcoded list of Austrian public holidays for 2026 and 2027 in `src/services/holidays.ts`, which `isBusinessDay` checks. It was built that way because the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet access, so it has to work fully offline.

### Q7
No. The ERP answers 422 to any array payload and only accepts a single event object per request. The user tried batching in September, so we did not build it.

### Q8
No new npm dependencies of any kind, not even dev dependencies. Every new package has to go through a security review, which takes about six weeks.

### Q9
Yes. I benchmarked it and found `calculateEta` isn't the bottleneck, so I never implemented memoization. The user later said QA found stale ETAs after new events and asked to remove the memoization completely. There was nothing in the repo to remove, so I only added a regression test. Caching ETAs is a dead end, and pagination of the list will come later.

### Q10
There are 3 attempts in total with a fixed 30 s delay and no exponential backoff. The ERP deduplicates by event_id only within a 2-minute window, so all attempts must land inside it. The delay is injectable for tests.

### Q11
Never log the recipient's name, address or phone number, because it is personal data under GDPR and the data protection officer flagged it in last month's audit. Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine to log.

### Q12
Yes, 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts, tracked as OPS-412. It fails about 1 in 5 runs because of a timer race in the fake notifier. If it fails, rerun once and don't try to fix it, because the platform team owns the fix.

### Q13
Only ATP (Austrian Post) numbers are validated. They must be valid UPU S10 numbers including the check digit, per docs/carriers.md. Other carriers accept any non-empty value, because their formats change too often and valid DHL numbers were rejected for two days last year.

### Q14
Nothing is built yet. `fs.watch` never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and file change events don't propagate into the container. Polling with `fs.watchFile` worked, so that is the way to go later.

### Q15
Yes, GET /shipments/:id. Mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields, and the next release isn't until January. The `eta` field was added only to the list, and a test guards the exact keys of the detail response.
